newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth bidding for Peru's Tele 2000.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth bidding for Peru's Tele 2000.

text.p: BellSouth Corp. is bidding for a majority stake in Peruvian cellular phone company Tele 2000 in a deal worth at least $100 million, its sixth in Latin America, the regional phone company confirmed Tuesday.
The Lima Stock Exchange first announced the bid for a 54 percent to 64 percent stake in Tele 2000 on Monday. Tele 2000 shareholders have 10 business days to sell their shares.

BellSouth has agreed to buy 38 percent of Tele 2000 from two major shareholders, including Tele 2000 Chairman Genaro Delgado Parker. If the offer is successful, the Atlanta-based company and Parker would jointly hold 90 percent or more of Tele 2000.
A 54 percent stake in the Peruvian company would be worth $100 million, BellSouth said.

Tele 2000 stock closed at 3.80 soles ($1.47) a share on the Lima exchange Monday. The market said BellSouth's offer worked out to 4.00 soles ($1.50) per share, based on an exchange rate of 2.67 soles to the dollar.
Tele 2000 shares rose 0.10 sole (4 cents) in morning trading on the exchange. BellSouth stock rose $1.50 to $40.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Lima market said BellSouth had been negotiating with Tele 2000 for more than a year. Tele 2000 holds rights to provide cellular service to Lima and parts of western Peru, and offers cable television and paging.
"We are comfortable operating in Latin America. The potential is certainly there and does seem to translate into real growth," a BellSouth spokesman said.
The Tele 2000 deal would give BellSouth its sixth Latin American wireless market. The Baby Bell already has stakes in companies in Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Venezuela and Panama.
